title: GitOpsVcsReplacement
description: Historical masterplan prerequisite for an Oyatie-owned VCS replacement. ADR-0363 and ADR-0515 supersede this as live coordination/merge authority; retained content is provenance and reusable design input for cloud-scm/cloud-ci/cloud-cd and the agentic delivery fabric.

user_directives_2026_05_14: move our vcs replacement for grit earlier
apply the same logic / feature as grit but upgrade it
currently it only works with local merges. I want it to be able to handle our gitops pipeline
look at what makes grit so good for agentic development in rust that avoids merge conflicts and avoids wasted work and integrated into our ci/cd pipeline
ci / cd, review & fix loop should be accounted for and it should handle the rebase and merge queue itself
Our project isn't pure rust; account for Swift, Kotlin, C#, C++/WinUI3, and other non-Rust surfaces.
Unit test, integration test, e2e test standard is established, documented, and enforced.
Still support Abstract Syntax Tree handling.
Oya VCS is our version of grit: an agent-native VCS/CI/CD coordination layer, not just local symbol locks.
GitHub and GitHub Actions are first-class adapters, but the same Oya VCS features must work without GitHub.
Trivy and Argo CD are current DevOps pipeline adapters; both remain replaceable because in-house options are expected later.
Think creatively about agentic development and keep the pipeline moving for long-compile languages like Rust.
Agents push/submit PR views at variable speeds, with many PRs per hour; Oya VCS must regulate throughput without stalling independent work.
Integrate with issue tracker through a GitHub Issues adapter while preserving provider-neutral issue tracking semantics.
_meta.design_posture: Historical provider-neutral Oya VCS core first. Superseded live posture: agents use plain git isolated worktree branches and protected PRs; cloud-ci gate apps produce oya-ci-required; GitHub/GitHub Actions, Trivy, Argo CD, GitLab, and future in-house systems are adapters or bridge/reference substrates, never replacement merge authority by themselves.
_meta.purpose: Historical masterplan prerequisite and provenance record for useful agentic-development semantics. It is not a current closure-authority contract: live closeout is plain git protected PR -> reviewer approval -> oya-ci-required -> release-governance/product-completion evidence.
_meta.supersession_boundary: ADR-0363 retires the bespoke Oya VCS/oya git ratchet; ADR-0515 makes cloud-ci gate apps behind the single protected oya-ci-required context the live CI/merge authority. Surviving Oya VCS and oya-vcs strings in this file are historical/provenance unless explicitly marked as migrated semantics.
user_directives_2026_05_15: grit, icm, rtk, vox, omx, and omc are being phased out; Oya VCS is set to replace them and must work seamlessly with the Foundry agentic pipeline.

moved_earlier_in_masterplan.ordering_rule: Historical P00 ordering record. P00 core design work is complete as provenance; forward closure authority is now plain git protected PRs plus reviewer approval and oya-ci-required, while Oya VCS/grit/icm-era surfaces remain compatibility/provenance only.
blocks: M01 shard fan-out beyond already-landed bootstrap work
moved_earlier_in_masterplan.rationale: The conflict-avoidance primitive must remain production/GitOps-capable before broad agent fan-out. Local merge serialization is not sufficient for Oyatie CI/CD; current ownership is plain git protected PR scope, reviewer approval, oya-ci-required, and cloud-ci/agentic-delivery-fabric semantics rather than the retired Oya VCS ratchet.

grit_capabilities_to_preserve.source_grit_feature: tree-sitter/AST symbol extraction; Rust functions, structs, enums, traits, impls, and types are lockable units
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.oyatie_upgrade: Preserve AST handling and generalize it: Rust AST remains first-class, while Swift/Kotlin/C#/C++/TypeScript/XAML and schema/config artifacts get language-native AST or parser-backed semantic symbols. Cargo/TOML, OpenAPI, JSON/YAML, Cedar, SQL, and CI files expose pointer/operation/policy/job symbols.
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.why_it_avoids_waste: Agents claim semantic AST/artifact units instead of line hunks or whole files, so unrelated edits in the same file or project can proceed in parallel.

grit_capabilities_to_preserve.source_grit_feature: claim locks symbols, work happens in isolated worktrees, done merges and releases
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.oyatie_upgrade: claim -> work -> verify -> done -> promote; done emits a signed ChangeBundle and promotion request instead of performing a local merge. Locks release only on accepted/published/rolled-back terminal states.
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.why_it_avoids_waste: Agents get isolated workspaces and deterministic closeout without throwing away completed feature work after hunk conflicts.

grit_capabilities_to_preserve.source_grit_feature: write locks, shared read locks, and dependency-aware locking
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.oyatie_upgrade: Dependency graph spans Rust AST edges plus contracts/schemas/docs/registry rows. A write claim on a public API automatically read-locks consumers and CI checks any unclaimed consumer drift.
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.why_it_avoids_waste: Downstream agents can keep working when only read stability is needed, while conflicting writers queue before producing incompatible edits.

grit_capabilities_to_preserve.source_grit_feature: queued contested claims, TTL heartbeat, watch events
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.oyatie_upgrade: Controller-backed leases with durable event stream (NATS/Kafka-compatible abstraction), stale-agent recovery, fairness policy, and CI-visible lock state.
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.why_it_avoids_waste: Blocked agents wait or get reassigned before spending tokens on work that cannot land.

grit_capabilities_to_preserve.source_grit_feature: local SQLite plus Azure Blob/S3-compatible conditional locks and events
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.oyatie_upgrade: Provider-neutral LockStorePort with local, S3/R2/MinIO, Postgres advisory-lock, and Kubernetes Lease adapters. Azure remains an adapter option, not the architectural center.
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.why_it_avoids_waste: Team/CI/remote agents share the same lock state instead of each machine believing it owns the merge lane.

grit_capabilities_to_preserve.source_grit_feature: serialized done prevents local index.lock races and merge conflicts
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.oyatie_upgrade: Serialized closeout is moved into a GitOps promotion queue. The controller owns remote branch/ref mutation, CI reruns, policy admission, environment promotion, rollback, and audit emission.
grit_capabilities_to_preserve.why_it_avoids_waste: Successful work is promoted by a single authority after gates pass; local agents no longer race each other or bypass CI/CD.

public_interface.compatibility_note: ADR-0116 retires grit/icm/rtk/vox as agent transition authorities; any legacy aliases are import/migration compatibility only and cannot be closure authority.

clean_architecture_rules: kernel has no git provider, CI provider, filesystem watcher, or network dependency
adapters own tree-sitter, lock backend, CI provider, and GitOps controller integration
controller performs remote repo mutations; agents never invoke git/gh
all state transitions are idempotent and audit-emitted
review/fix/rebase/merge-queue code lives in application/adapters; kernel only models states and invariants
polyglot indexers are adapters behind PolyglotIndexPort; Rust-first assumptions must not leak into the kernel
all protected-branch publication is controller-owned and merge-queue mediated
unit/integration/e2e standards are admission gates, not advisory docs
AST handling remains a core capability for semantic locks, impacted tests, review mapping, and conflict detection

pipeline_shape: agent claims semantic symbols across Rust/TS/Swift/Kotlin/C#/C++/XAML/schema/config surfaces
done packages signed ChangeBundle instead of local merge
admission controller verifies claim coverage, no forbidden direct tool use, tests, policy, provenance, and bundle integrity
review/fix loop runs as typed controller-managed tasks until accepted or rejected
controller refreshes/rebases bundle onto protected branch state and reruns affected gates
controller enrolls accepted bundle into merge queue
CI/CD gates run from merge queue state
GitOps reconciler promotes accepted state to environments
controller emits terminal event and releases or rolls back locks

admission_gates.rule: Every changed symbol/path/artifact pointer must be covered by an active write claim or generated by an allowed generator.
CI fails bundles with unclaimed semantic diffs, including docs/specs/registries.
Agent-authored logs/evidence must show no direct git/gh calls outside controller identity.
Index generation timestamp must be newer than bundle base revision or explicitly reconciled.
Run targeted gates, affected dependency tests, active-artifact contract, architecture/doc coverage, and configured pipeline lanes before promotion.
Bundle has agent id, claim ids, test evidence, source digest, signature, and audit-chain event id.
Every reviewer-requested or CI-requested change maps to a typed FixupTask, scoped symbols, evidence, and terminal state.
Bundles reaching merge queue must be rebased/refreshed by controller identity, never agent shell commands.
Protected-branch publication occurs through the controller-managed merge queue with policy evidence.
Non-Rust changes require claim coverage from language/config-specific indexers, not file-only fallback unless the artifact type is intentionally file-scoped.
docs/standards/testing.md, /specs/test-standard.json, and /registry/test-set-registry.json exist before P00 exits.
Unit/integration/e2e required tiers are derived from semantic diff and enforced before merge queue promotion.
Required tier evidence must be fresh after controller-owned rebase/patch replay.
AST/parser-backed symbols are available for all supported language surfaces or the artifact kind declares an intentional file/pointer scope.

Every promoted ChangeBundle must attach a multispectrum evidence file covering required F-family, A-family, and M-family facets for the changeset scope; missing or incomplete evidence rejects promotion.

Retired by ADR-0363/ADR-0515: do not require or bless an Oya VCS CLI claim/work/verify/done/promote surface as live authority. Any remaining local wrapper is migration/provenance evidence only; gate semantics must live in cloud-ci/Rust packets behind oya-ci-required.
Promotion evidence must include passed CI, GitHub Actions, Trivy, and Argo GitOps provider slots or an explicitly approved native replacement slot.
Every attached multispectrum evidence file must have an audit-chain row keyed by the same change_id before promotion.

gitops_pipeline_integration.lock_release_policy: Release on accepted/published/rolled-back/rejected terminal event. Keep or downgrade lock while a fixup is queued if the controller can preserve queue fairness without blocking unrelated symbols.
controller_owned_operations: merge queue enrollment and status watch

implementation_plan.deliverable: Language-agnostic kernel model + symbol graph schema + claim/queue/lease invariants; Rust AST remains first-class, not exclusive.
Local + distributed LockStorePort adapters and watch event stream.
Signed ChangeBundle format with claim coverage manifest and evidence records.
Controller-owned remote promotion path integrated with CI/CD admission, review/fix loop, rebase, merge queue, and environment reconciliation.
Grit-compatible CLI aliases, migration from local grit, CI ratchet banning local-only closeout for agent fan-out.
Swift/Kotlin/C#/C++/XAML/TypeScript/config/contract semantic indexers with cross-language dependency edges.
Typed review/fix loop plus controller-owned rebase and merge queue orchestration, with CI/CD evidence and terminal states.
Document and machine-encode unit/integration/e2e standards, registry-driven commands, and CI/CD admission enforcement.
Language-neutral AST symbol/range/dependency contract used by claims, review mapping, impacted tests, and semantic conflict checks.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Preserves useful local conflict avoidance but cannot own remote GitOps promotion, environment reconciliation, or CI/CD admission.
Line/hunk-level conflicts and branch/PR race conditions still waste agent work before CI sees semantic intent.
Conflict prevention is already solved by symbol locks; upgrade the closeout/promotion boundary instead of rebuilding redundant coordination.

review_fix_loop.owner: GitOps VCS controller; agents provide patches/fixups but do not rebase, merge, push, or manipulate PRs directly.
loop_rules: Reviewer comments and CI failures become typed FixupTasks linked to original claim ids and affected symbols.
Controller grants fixup claims for only the symbols implicated by comments/failures unless impact analysis widens the scope.
Fixup bundles are layered on top of the original ChangeBundle and preserve provenance rather than discarding prior agent work.
Controller reruns targeted checks first, then merge-queue/full gates as configured.
Every loop iteration emits review, fix, CI, rebase, queue, and promotion evidence.
review_fix_loop.waste_avoidance: Review and CI failures do not force agents to restart from scratch; they become scoped fixup tasks with preserved bundle history.

rebase_and_merge_queue.semantic_conflict_policy: If a text rebase succeeds but claimed semantic symbols conflict with a newly-landed bundle, queue a typed review/fix task instead of publishing.
rebase_and_merge_queue.merge_queue_policy: Single controller serializes protected-branch publication. Agents can observe queue state but cannot reorder, force, or bypass it.

test_standard_enforcement.objective: Unit, integration, and e2e test standards are established, documented, machine-readable, and enforced by the VCS/GitOps admission path before broad agent fan-out.

documentation_artifacts.purpose: Machine-readable standard consumed by admission gates and CI/CD templates.
Per-language/test-set inventory: owner, command, scope, required trigger, flake budget, artifact outputs.

test_tiers.definition: Pure or tightly-scoped component tests with no network/external service dependency; fastest proof for changed logic.
required_for: all changed semantic symbols with executable logic

test_tiers.definition: Boundary tests across ports/adapters/storage/contracts with controlled local dependencies and deterministic fixtures.
User/workflow-level tests across deployed or preview composition, including desktop/mobile/web flows where relevant.

admission_rules: ChangeBundle must declare affected test tiers derived from semantic diff and dependency graph.
Admission rejects bundles missing required unit/integration/e2e commands for their affected surfaces.
Review/fix loop must attach failing test evidence to typed FixupTasks.
Merge queue promotion requires required tier evidence fresh after controller-owned rebase.

E2E gaps may be gap_accepted_with_reason only when the spec marks the surface non-user-facing or platform verification is impossible in current runner; gap must block production promotion if user-facing.

flake_policy.rerun_policy: Controller may retry known flaky e2e once, but cannot convert persistent failure to pass.

product_definition.name: Historical Oya VCS
product_definition.one_liner: Historical agent-native semantic VCS/CI/CD coordination design that queued ChangeSets, not just branches or PRs.
product_definition.core_thesis: Historical Oya VCS design preserved grit-style AST/symbol conflict avoidance, then added provider-neutral ChangeSets, virtual merge stacks, queue-aware locks, review/CI fix loops, and dev→staging→production promotion.
product_definition.not_a_git_replacement: Historical Oya VCS design orchestrated Git-compatible storage, CI, review, security scanning, merge queues, and GitOps environments through ports/adapters; the useful semantic state machine concepts are provenance for current cloud-scm/cloud-ci/cloud-cd work.
must_provide_same_features_without_provi: security scan admission through local or in-house scanner adapter
GitOps promotion through local or in-house reconciler adapter

ChangeSet.semantics: The queue item is a semantic ChangeSet with symbol/test/dependency knowledge, not just a PR or branch name.

VirtualHead.semantics: Speculative queue projection used for CI and unlock decisions before target branch mutation.

QueueAwareLease.unlock_rule: A conflicting next agent may receive the symbol once the current ChangeSet is queue-stable and the next agent rebases onto the correct virtual predecessor, not only after physical merge.

ReleaseTrain.semantics: Promotion moves lineage-aware ChangeSets through dev, staging, and production without naive cherry-pick blindness.

native_and_adapter_boundary.principle: Historical design principle: product semantics lived in Oya VCS kernel/application ports. Current live authority is plain git protected PRs plus cloud-ci/oya-ci; reusable provider-adapter semantics may migrate into cloud-scm/cloud-ci/cloud-cd.

native_mode.queue_backend: Local/provider-neutral queue store with durable JSON/event-log or embedded database implementation; remote backends plug in through QueueStorePort.
native_mode.ci_backend: Local command runner and evidence collector can execute the same TestStandardPort gates without GitHub Actions.
native_mode.review_backend: Native review task store can model comments/approvals/fixups without GitHub PRs.
native_mode.security_backend: Native/in-house scan adapter can satisfy SecurityScanPort when Trivy is absent.
native_mode.gitops_backend: Native/in-house reconciler adapter can satisfy GitOpsReconcilerPort when Argo CD is absent.
native_mode.merge_queue_backend: Native semantic queue can construct virtual heads and release locks even when provider merge queues are unavailable.

native_and_adapter_boundary.adapter_parity_rule: Historical parity rule: every first-class adapter mapped provider concepts into Oya VCS ChangeSet/VirtualHead/FixupTask/ReleaseTrain states and could not remove native capabilities.

required_capabilities: distinguish PR vs merge_group vs environment jobs
first_class_adapters.native_equivalent: LocalCiAdapter or future OyaActionsAdapter must provide same CiProvider contract.

GitOpsReconcilerPort consumes desired/live/reconciled/drifted/failed states; Argo-specific CRDs stay adapter-local.

maps: issue comments ↔ requirement updates or review/fix context
first_class_adapters.spam_control: Use marker comments and digest updates; do not post one noisy issue comment per queue transition when many PRs/hour are flowing.

virtual_merge_stack.description: Build ordered projections H0 + C1 = H1, H1 + C2 = H2, etc. Required checks run against virtual heads. A failed ChangeSet invalidates only dependent later ChangeSets when semantic fingerprints prove independence.
virtual_merge_stack.artifact_reuse_rule: Targeted and full-check artifacts may be reused only when toolchain, dependency graph, semantic diff fingerprint, feature set, environment, and predecessor virtual head are compatible.

queue_aware_locks.early_unlock_rule: Release a symbol to the next waiting agent at queue-stable when review approved, required CI green, patch applies cleanly to current virtual queue head, and no higher-priority conflicting ChangeSet remains ahead.
queue_aware_locks.wrong_base_prevention: Agents never rebase onto raw target branch; they receive the queue projection containing required predecessors.

queue_model.failure_minimization: When a ChangeSet fails, remove or quarantine it, compute semantic dependency impact on later items, rebase independent items onto the last good virtual head, and rerun only invalidated checks before final full gate.

rust_compile_latency_strategy.goal: Keep agents and queues moving despite long Rust compile times by separating confidence tiers, warming builds, reusing valid artifacts, and unlocking on queue-stable virtual heads.

validation_ladder.purpose: Reject obvious bad ChangeSets in seconds without invoking rustc.
Catch type errors before full test build.

runs: property tests for changed state machines
validation_ladder.purpose: Give quick confidence tied to semantic diff.
Protect downstream crates without full workspace by default.

runs: workspace required tests on virtual queue head
validation_ladder.purpose: Final queue admission before target mutation.

compile_avoidance_and_reuse: Compile futures: start low-risk cargo check/test jobs as soon as ChangeSet is submitted, before review finishes.
Build-warm leases: hold warm builder pools keyed by rustc version, Cargo.lock hash, feature set, target triple, profile, and virtual-head fingerprint.
Semantic artifact cache: reuse test/build artifacts only if changed symbols, dependency closure, features, env, and predecessor stack are unchanged.
Critical-path scheduler: ingest cargo --timings reports to identify bottleneck crates and schedule queue order around compile heat.
Reverse-dep minimizer: public API changes fan out; private function changes stay crate-local until virtual-head full gate.
Feature hygiene gate: detect accidental all-features/default-feature explosion and duplicate dependency versions before CI waste.
build.rs invalidation guard: require precise rerun-if-changed hints for build scripts that otherwise invalidate whole packages.
Compile slot economy: queue owns scarce full-build slots; agents get cheap L0-L2 feedback while waiting.
Speculative sibling batching: independent ChangeSets can share a virtual head/full build when semantic dependency fingerprints are disjoint and batching does not delay hotfixes.
Rust compile doctor: map compiler/test failures to crate/symbol/test, create FixupTask, and keep unrelated queue items moving.
rust_compile_latency_strategy.long_compile_failure_policy: Historical design rule: a long-running full Rust gate could not hold unrelated independent ChangeSets indefinitely; the retired Oya VCS plan would split the queue, reuse safe artifacts, or demote the slow item to fixup/quarantine when policy permitted. Current work should express this through cloud-ci/agentic-delivery-fabric scheduling semantics.

failure_mode_synthesis.purpose: Historical failure-mode synthesis: what could go wrong, how Oya VCS would detect it, what fixes were automated, and when escalation was required. Retained as provenance for current cloud-ci/agentic-delivery-fabric semantics.

high_throughput_agent_scheduler.problem: Agents complete work and submit PR views at variable speeds, potentially many per hour, while Rust and polyglot CI gates complete much slower. Without a scheduler, fast agents can flood review/CI/merge queues and slow agents can hold stale locks.
high_throughput_agent_scheduler.unit_of_flow: ChangeSet; provider PRs are views/materializations, not the scheduling unit.
core_mechanisms: PR aperture: cap open provider PR views per lane; keep excess ChangeSets native/queued until review or provider visibility is useful.
Token buckets per scarce resource: compile slots, full CI slots, review capacity, provider API calls, merge queue positions, GitOps promotion lanes.
Adaptive batching: independent small ChangeSets may share a provider PR/merge group/release train while retaining separate ChangeSet lineage and rollback metadata.
Stale-risk scoring: older ChangeSets, wrong-base work, public API changes, and dependency updates get refreshed before expensive CI.
Sprint/slowpoke fairness: fast agents cannot starve older/high-priority work; slow agents must heartbeat or their claims become reassignment candidates.
Work stealing: queued/failing fixup tasks can be reassigned to idle agents with compatible symbol/indexer capabilities.
Provider backpressure: GitHub/API/Actions/rate-limit or review overload shifts ChangeSets to native queue mode without losing status.
Hotfix bypass with semantic proof: security/production fixes can jump lanes only if dependency graph shows safe bypass or policy records explicit invalidation cost.
Queue compaction: docs/copy/config-only independent ChangeSets may batch; high-risk kernel/API/security changes stay isolated.
Digest reporting: issues/PRs receive summarized state updates to avoid comment spam during many-PR/hour bursts.

many_prs_per_hour_policy.dedupe: Duplicate issue comments/events do not create duplicate FixupTasks.

CI and branch protection must expose oya-ci-required as the single required status before broad fan-out.
Provider adapters are replaceable; core invariants remain provider-neutral and testable locally.

keep Foundry agentic throughput high without allowing local-only closeout
